name: PT Petrosea Tbk

frontmatter.title: Petrosea — a contract book priced for a recovery the cash flow has not delivered
frontmatter.summary: Petrosea is the Barito group's mining-contractor and EPC vehicle — a record order book, a fleet-heavy balance sheet and an equity trading well above our fundamental value. We hold HOLD with a target of Rp2,065; the konglo lens keeps part of the premium for twelve months, so the expected return is price-only and negative.
thesis: Petrosea is a contract business, not a coal producer — the coal deck reaches it through client capex and award timing, not through a selling price of its own [S2][S4].

The order book is the strong part — US$4,439.0m of unsatisfied obligations at end-FY2025 plus two life-of-mine contracts signed in July 2026 worth US$431.2m and US$89.6m — but conversion is capital-hungry and interest now absorbs most of EBIT [S3][S4].
At Rp2,250 the shares trade at 2.5x the probability-weighted fundamental value of Rp912.1; the lens closes 30.0% of the log premium in its base regime, giving Rp2,065 and -8.2% [S10][S11].
The reverse DCF says the price needs FY2027E revenue growth near 21.0% against our 8.0%; that gap, not the coal price, is the call [S0][S4].

catalysts.event: Extraordinary shareholders' meeting on the proposed rights issue
MSCI consultation feedback deadline on Indonesia's Standalone-status proposal
MSCI decision on Indonesia's market classification

blocks.text: **What changed.** We now carry the SINI stake of 19.9% at cost, not at the 6 November market quote: SINI is an uncovered Hapsoro-group konglo sibling and the konglo card's sibling rule bars a market mark inside fundamental value. We add the KMS collection residual to the bridge and restate FY2025 interest from the LK so the history foots. The target is now Rp2,065, *below* the previous target; nothing operating changed, and the 23 November EGM is the next dated event [S3][S5][S11]. The 5 November reclassification of PTRO into other metals stays flagged to the Director, and the peer cohort stays pinned to contractor and energy-services names [S4].

**The call.** HOLD, twelve-month target Rp2,065 against Rp2,250, total return -8.2%. The modelled dividend over the next twelve months is Rp0, so the return is price-only [S0]. The target is not fundamental value — it is the konglo lens's most-likely price, which keeps part of the premium and closes it gradually [S10][S11]. The shares can trade below target and still sit far above fundamental value.

Petrosea is an Indonesian engineering, construction and mining-services company with four disclosed revenue lines — Mining, Construction and Engineering, EPCI-Offshore Oil and Gas, and Services — plus a small at-a-point-in-time coal-sale line [S4]. It works for coal miners in Kalimantan and Sumatra and for mineral producers including Vale Indonesia and Freeport [S2][S4]. The model is contract-based and capital-intensive — it is paid for overburden removal, coal hauling, mine development and construction — so the KPIs that matter are overburden volume and coal production, 135.2 million BCM and 19.2 million tonnes in FY2025 [S2].

The strategy is to convert the order book into long-life contracts and diversify the customer and commodity mix. At end-FY2025 the company disclosed US$4,439.0m of unsatisfied performance obligations, dominated by Mining, and expects US$1,134.7m of it to be recognised in 2026 [S4]. In July 2026 it added two coal-mining services agreements in Kapuas, Central Kalimantan: PT Pesona Bara Cakrawala for US$431.2m over the life of mine and PT Cakrawala Bara Persada for US$89.6m. These are third-party awards: the contract note lists PBC and CBP only as counterparties, and the H1 2026 related-party note does not name them [S3]. The non-coal thrust appears in the same record: the INPEX Masela OLNG contract of Rp989.0bn to March 2029, the Reko Diq earthworks contract of US$17.5m, and the HBS gold-services contracts, HBS acquired at an estimated US$25.8m in 2025 [S3][S2]. The base credits the disclosed PBC, CBP, INPEX and Reko Diq values over their terms as the FY2027 step; HBS revenue is undisclosed and the gold/copper work is a bull case.

The controlling shareholder is PT Kreasi Jasa Persada (KJP) with 45.3% at end-February 2026; PT Caraka Reksa Optima held 24.4% and the public 30.1% [S2]. KJP is a subsidiary of PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) and the beneficial owner is Prajogo Pangestu [S2]. The Sinergi coal transaction is a **cross-group** deal — PT Singaraja Putra (SINI) belongs to the Hapsoro group, not the Barito group [S11]. SINI bought the KMS coal mine in June 2026 for a transaction value of US$97.0m, and Petrosea subscribed US$65.8m to the SINI rights issue on 23 July 2026 for 19.9%, which makes SINI a related-party associate from that date. The flag attaches to the associate relationship and the KMS receivable, not to PBC and CBP [S3][S11].

Mining services is a scale business: contractors compete on fleet availability, utilisation, safety record, stripping cost per BCM and the ability to finance equipment against multi-year contracts. Petrosea sits in the large-contract tier, and its position rests on the owned fleet, Barito-group customer access and a long record in coal and mineral projects [S2]. The demand driver is not the spot coal price but miners' stripping and development budgets: when prices fall, clients defer overburden and awards, and the reverse happens with a lag [S4][S7]. The house coal deck prices Newcastle at US$118/t for FY2027E against US$150/t spot [S13], a demand signal and one reason our growth moderates after FY2026E even with a large order book. The oil deck's Brent path reaches costs through diesel and equipment rental, so we model a narrow cost link with partial pass-through [S4].

Regulation is the main external swing factor. From 1 January 2027 strategic-resource exports, including coal, must go through the state exporter PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia under Permendag No. 15/2026 and PP No. 24/2026; existing Eksportir Terdaftar coal licences expire at the end of 2026 and participants have warned that administration could be disrupted at the changeover [S7]. Petrosea's revenue is mostly domestic service revenue, so the direct effect is limited, but the rule affects clients' export logistics and award timing. The market regime is hostile to concentrated-ownership names — HSC stocks are out of the IHSG calculation and MSCI opened a Standalone consultation [S8][S9] — a valuation variable, not an operating one.

Contract tenors are long — the Kapuas agreements run for the life of the mine and the legacy Vale, Kideco and Barasentosa contracts to dates between 2028 and 2034 — so the battle is fought at award [S2][S3]. Petrosea does not disclose a share of the listed contractor pool; it is a large-contract specialist with an owned fleet, a real but narrow advantage because clients can re-tender or split work at each renewal [S2][S4]. The moat is moderate at best: long-life contracts, switching costs and fleet scale protect the incumbent, but the business is cyclical, capital-intensive and concentrated. Buyer power is unfavourable, incumbency favourable, new entry neutral-to-unfavourable; group ROE has been in the single digits through the cycle [S4].

FY2025 revenue was US$886.5m, up from US$690.8m, and gross profit US$112.2m against US$90.3m [S4]. The consolidated figure included US$52.0m of at-a-point-in-time KMS coal sales, divested on 30 June 2026; revenue recognised over time, the continuing base the forecast carries, was US$834.4m [S4]. Management expects US$1,134.7m to be recognised in 2026 — 28.0% above the consolidated audited base but faster on the continuing base, because the forecast has no coal-sales line [S3][S4]. Gross margin fell to 12.7% from 13.1% as the mix shifted to lower-margin EPC and new mining work, and H1 2026 printed US$47.0m on US$544.0m [S3][S4]. Depreciation of US$90.6m and amortisation of US$14.6m were charged in FY2025; the data pack's D&A is a fraction of that — a direct-method cash-flow artefact — so we restate it from the notes: FY2025A EBITDA is US$162.9m after the final tax of US$9.7m the LK reports inside operating costs, and FY2024A restates to US$96.5m on the same definition [S4].

**Gross margin, input versus realised.** The 9.7% input is a pre-link figure at base input costs; the Brent cost link is applied on top, so the realised line is 8.8% in FY2026E, 10.2% in FY2027E and 12.4% in FY2030E [S4]. The link exposes 5.0% of COGS to Brent with a 50.0% pass-through, our central case; no disclosed clause quantifies it [S4].

**Balance sheet and forecast.** Capex of US$434.3m against operating cash flow of US$48.2m produced negative free cash flow, and debt rose to US$849.6m against cash of US$72.0m; interest and finance charges were US$55.7m in FY2025, restated from the LK so the history foots [S4]. At 30 June 2026 interim cash was US$80.4m with the KMS current receivable on the balance sheet, and H1 capex was US$43.1m of PP&E plus US$4.0m of intangibles — the 8.7% run-rate we hold for the year [S3].

**Forecast.** Revenue grows 28.0% to US$1,134.7m — the level management states — then 8.0%, 7.0%, 5.0% and 4.0% as the RPO converts; no volume decline is assumed and the undisclosed Petrindo pipeline and HBS contracts stay out. SG&A plus final tax is held at 4.5% of revenue and capex at the H1 run-rate rising to 11.0% long run, in line with D&A [S3][S4]. EBITDA rises from US$184.7m to US$270.5m, but interest of US$68.0m keeps pre-tax profit negative in FY2026E; parent net profit is US$-16.2m in FY2026E, US$2.2m in FY2027E and materially positive by FY2028E [S3][S4].

**Earnings quality.** The cash test is clean — operating cash flow exceeded net profit in FY2023 (US$107.8m against US$12.2m), FY2024 (US$27.9m against US$9.7m) and FY2025 (US$48.2m against US$28.8m) — so the accruals ratio is negative in all three years; the reader can rebuild it from total assets of US$728.0m, US$867.3m and US$1,582.9m [S2][S4]. The real flag is the one-off: FY2025 other gains of US$34.5m were almost the whole pre-tax profit of US$39.3m, so recurring earnings were a small fraction of reported US$28.8m, and we set other non-operating income to zero from FY2026E [S4]. The related-party channel is material and we read it as optics-class — revenue was US$109.6m, or 12.4% of the total, in FY2025 and US$96.5m, or 17.8%, in H1 2026, and related-party trade receivables of US$103.5m plus US$89.9m of other current were 6.8% of consolidated assets [S3][S4]. The KMS sale was booked at a US$5.8m loss, so it did not flatter earnings, and the current receivable was collected in July 2026. Both are optics-class — disclosed, priced and reported, with no manipulation finding and no special notation in the record [S0].
The method set is the MINING_CONTRACTORS house set — an FCFF DCF primary, EV/EBITDA and EV/Sales cross-checks — because a contractor is valued on the cash its contract book generates after capex.
We drop the P/E leg: FY2025A parent net profit of US$28.8m includes a US$34.5m non-recurring gain, so trailing P/E capitalises a one-off peak [S4].

**Weights.** DCF 65.0%, EV/EBITDA 25.0%, EV/Sales 10.0%. EV/Sales is the worse: its FY2025A revenue metric of US$886.5m still contains the US$52.0m of divested KMS coal sales, so on the continuing base of US$834.4m it overstates value and we treat its output as an upper bound [S4]. EV/EBITDA runs on restated trailing EBITDA after the US$9.7m final tax the peers exclude, so it is a floor [S4].

The WACC is built from a USD risk-free rate, the house mature-market ERP and Indonesia country risk premium, with an unlevered beta of 1.00 — the industry default in the house configuration, not a company source — levered to 1.52 at the company's debt-to-equity ratio and a pre-tax debt cost of 6.9%, giving a cost of equity of 15.0% and a WACC of 11.2% [S12].

The DCF gives an enterprise value of US$987.1m and Rp559 per share, with terminal value at 45.2% of the total. A life-end DCF with no terminal value produces a non-positive equity value, so we keep the terminal value and disclose its weight [S0]. **Valuation date.** The bridge uses the 30 June 2026 balance sheet, a mid-year value while the price is 4 November 2026; rolling to the price date would add roughly four months of the cost of capital, which does not change the call [S3]. Cash in the bridge is US$80.4m plus other financial assets of US$11.1m. The bridge carries the SINI stake at cost, the non-current KMS receivable of US$12.4m, and the current receivable's collection residual — the US$97.0m disposal value less the US$65.8m subscription and that non-current receivable [S3]. The BCA bridging time loan was drawn only on 13 July and 17 July 2026 (US$84.0m) and repaid in full on 24 July 2026, so it is not in the 30 June net debt; the US$84.7m current receivable was collected the same day and the drawdown and repayment net to zero [S3]. The SINI stake is held at cost because SINI is an uncovered Hapsoro-group konglo sibling, and the 6 November quote is disclosed as a sensitivity rather than a fundamental mark [S11].

**Cross-checks.** EV/EBITDA at 7.5x gives Rp989, 76.9% above the DCF; EV/Sales at 1.2x gives Rp766, 37.0% above it. The gap is expected — the multiples capitalise pre-capex, pre-interest value while the DCF deducts both [S0]. ATLA and PKPK are excluded: a subsea inspection contractor and a small cap whose multiple rests on near-zero trailing EBITDA, both at the top of the spread. DEWA (PT Darma Henwa) and MYOH (PT Samindo Resources) are retained as the closest coal-mining contractors, with UNIQ, WINS, RUIS and SUNI; the median, not the mean, is the anchor, and the metrics are FY2025A and labelled trailing [S0][S4].

Capex is the largest single sensitivity, recorded in the assumptions against DCF equity value [S4]. On the weights above, fundamental value today is Rp687 and probability-weighting the twelve-month business scenarios gives Rp1,046, below the market price [S0].

**The konglo lens.** At Rp2,250 the shares trade at 2.5x the probability-weighted fundamental value of Rp912.1 (0.90 in log terms) [S0][S11]. The house konglo lens keeps part of that gap for twelve months: target equals fundamental value times the probability-weighted share of the premium kept. With no regime flags the base regime closes 30.0% of the log gap and gives Rp1,967, the bear closes 70.0% and gives Rp1,371, and the bull lets the premium re-expand (-15.0%) to Rp2,954; on the deck's regime weights the target is Rp2,065, above the twelve-month fundamental value of Rp1,046. It is not a constrained-float squeeze — free float is 27.6%, above the minimum, with no HSC listing, index deletion or enforcement on record [S0][S11] — and the risks section states the full-closure downside alongside it.

**Leverage.** Interest of US$68.0m against EBIT of US$48.5m keeps pre-tax profit negative; H1 2026 showed a continuing profit only with non-recurring other gains [S3][S4]. **Covenants.** At 30 June 2026 loans fall due as US$56.5m within a year, US$322.4m in one to five years and US$199.3m beyond, alongside US$109.3m of bonds; the senior loans carry a debt-to-equity ceiling of 3.0x and an EBITDA-to-debt-and-interest floor of 115%, the bonds an EBITDA-to-interest-and-instalments floor of 1.15x, and the ANZ HBS facility needed a June 2026 waiver [S3]. **Margin.** New EPC and mining work mobilises at lower margins — the H1 2026 print of US$47.0m on US$544.0m is the evidence [S3][S4]. **Regulation.** The PT DSI export channel from 1 January 2027 could delay clients' exports and award timing [S7]. **Regime.** The MSCI Standalone consultation, the IHSG exclusion and the free-float roadmap can compress the konglo premium faster than our lens assumes [S8][S9]. **Counterparty.** Related-party revenue was 17.8% of H1 2026 revenue and US$103.5m plus US$89.9m of related-party receivables remain, so a collection delay is a cash risk [S3].

The business scenarios mirror four drivers: revenue growth, gross margin, cost of debt and working capital. The bear cuts growth and margin, resets the debt cost higher and adds a working-capital drag, valuing the equity at Rp372; the bull mirrors all four at Rp2,230; the base is Rp790, with probabilities of 25.0%, 50.0% and 25.0% [S0]. **The receivable and covenant stress is inside the bear, not beside it.** The working-capital shock is worth a little under half of the combined trade and other current related-party book — most of the trade receivable alone — and it is a permanent cash loss, not a write-off that reverses. The covenant and acceleration case rides the cost-of-debt shock: a reset, a waiver fee and tighter amortisation [S3].

The konglo regimes are separate — base Rp1,967, bear Rp1,371, bull Rp2,954, weighted to Rp2,065 [S10][S11]. **Full premium closure.** The lens bear still keeps 70.0% of the log gap, so the floor case is the twelve-month fundamental value itself, Rp1,046, against Rp2,250; the lens is an expectation about twelve months, not a claim the premium cannot go to zero. Why the base closes 30.0% rather than nothing: the premium is register-driven — two controlling blocks hold most of the shares, the group has an active capital-markets agenda (the KMS sale, the SINI rights issue, the 23 November EGM on a 1.7% rights issue) and traded supply is thin though compliant [S2][S3][S5].

**The bull, and what is not in it.** The bull mirrors the bear's shocks. PBC discloses life-of-mine overburden of 189 million BCM and coal production of 42 million tonnes against US$431.2m, and CBP discloses its own volumes against US$89.6m [S3]; a faster ramp than the base's 8.0% is what the growth shock proxies. The HBS gold and copper contracts and the Petrindo pipeline are *not* sized — neither carries a disclosed value, and an unsourced revenue number in a probability-weighted scenario is worse than leaving it out [S2][S3].

Signposts: a faster ramp of PBC/CBP, INPEX or Reko Diq would lift the revenue and margin path; approval of the rights issue would fund working capital but not repair the balance sheet — at 170m new shares it is 1.7% of paid-up capital and dilutes non-participants by at most 1.7% [S5]. An MSCI decision to keep Indonesia in Emerging Markets would slow compression; an adverse decision, a covenant tightening or a new related-party receivable would compress the lens and fundamental value together [S3][S7][S9][S10].

Petrosea is a konglo name in the registry — controller Prajogo Pangestu through KJP and CUAN, group role the listed mining contractor and EPC arm, holding 19.9% of SINI after the July 2026 rights issue [S2][S3][S11]. Ownership is concentrated (KJP 45.3%, CARA 24.4%, public 30.1%) and free float is 27.6%, above the minimum and compliant [S0][S2][S11]. The lens applies its default compression with no regime adjustment [S10][S11].

The related-party channel is the main governance fact and it is a cross-group one. SINI, a Hapsoro-group company, bought KMS at a transaction value of US$97.0m, booked at a US$5.8m loss, paid partly through a current receivable collected in July 2026 and a non-current receivable of US$12.4m due in 2027; Petrosea then subscribed US$65.8m to the SINI rights issue for 19.9% [S3][S11]. The stake makes SINI a related-party associate on a negotiated cross-group price, not an intra-group transfer. Related-party revenue was US$109.6m, or 12.4% of revenue, in FY2025 and US$96.5m, or 17.8%, in H1 2026, and related-party trade receivables were US$103.5m plus US$89.9m of other current, 6.8% of consolidated assets against US$321.3m of equity [S4][S3]. We classify the transaction as disclosed and optics-class, not manipulation-class — the sale was at a small loss, the current receivable was collected, and the stake is carried at cost in our bridge with the market quote disclosed as a sensitivity — but concentration of revenue, receivables and equity in group counterparties is a structural discount the lens captures [S3][S10].

Dividends were US$9.9m in FY2025 and US$3.1m in FY2024, about a third of parent net profit, but the debt and capex programme means the dividend is not the coal-producer anchor; the proposed November 2026 rights issue would fund working capital and dilute non-participants by at most 1.7% [S4][S5]. The auditor's opinion is unmodified with no down-tier or special notation in the archived filings [S0][S4]; we have not verified pledge status, so we make no statement on pledges. ESG exposures are the standard contractor set — safety, mine-site rehabilitation, diesel-fleet emissions and community relations — with no quantified target that would change the valuation [S2].

The dated catalysts are the 23 November 2026 EGM on the proposed rights issue and the 30 April 2027 and 30 June 2027 MSCI consultation and decision dates [S5][S9]. The non-current KMS receivable of US$12.4m falls due in 2027 and the INPEX OLNG contract runs to 1 March 2029 [S3].

The KPIs we watch are overburden removal and coal production (FY2025 — 135.2 million BCM and 19.2 million tonnes) [S2]; revenue conversion against the US$4,439.0m order book [S4]; gross margin, which printed US$47.0m on US$544.0m in H1 2026 [S3]; net debt, interest cover and the US$109.3m of bonds, with covenant tests; the related-party receivables; and the free-float, HSC and MSCI signals [S8][S9][S11]. A sustained gross margin above 10.7% with positive free cash flow would be the first evidence the base case is too cautious; a further related-party receivable would be the first evidence it is too optimistic.

bear.narrative: Coal prices undershoot the house deck, clients defer overburden and new awards, the new EPC/mining contracts mobilise at lower margins, the enlarged debt stack resets 150bp higher at refinancing under the D/E and EBITDA-to-debt covenants, and a quarter of the related-party trade receivable book is impaired rather than merely slow, absorbing cash.

bull.narrative: Coal demand holds above the deck, the PBC/CBP, INPEX and Reko Diq awards ramp faster with the enlarged fleet utilised, the HBS gold/copper contracts with Harmony Gold, Newmont and St Barbara convert into new awards, margins beat, refinancing lands at a lower cost and collections improve.

groups.name: Barito group (Prajogo Pangestu)
groups.role: mining contractor and EPC; holds 19.88% of SINI

events.note: sold its KMS coal mine to SINI (about Rp1.73tn) and took 19.88% of SINI

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is management's own revenue expectation, stated verbatim in Note 30 as US$1,135m of revenue to be recognised in 2026 (S4 p.118; F66); the +28.0% consolidated and +36.0% continuing-base growth rates are our derivations, not a management-stated percentage. The continuing base excludes the US$52.0m of divested KMS coal sales (S4 p.117; F38/F39). FY2027E 8% is the annualised contribution of the post-balance-sheet awards (PBC US$431.2m and CBP US$89.6m over life of mine, INPEX Rp989bn to 2029, Reko Diq US$17.5m) on top of that base; FY2028-30 moderate to 7/5/4% as the multi-year RPO converts. The path is not below the RPO conversion pace; management's 2026 expectation absorbs US$1,135m of the US$4,438.952m end-2025 book, so the remaining book supports the mid-single-digit path without a lost contract or a volume decline. The house coal deck's lower forward Newcastle path (FY2027E 118.0 vs spot 150.35, S13) is a second-order demand signal for a contractor, not the revenue driver. The undisclosed Petrindo-group pipeline (S2 p.20) and the HBS gold/copper contracts are excluded because no contract values are disclosed.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: H1 2026 gross margin was 8.65% as new EPC and mining contracts mobilised at lower initial margins; we hold 9.7% for FY2026E (H2 fleet utilisation improves) and recover to the FY2025 actual 12.66% by 2030 as the new life-of-mine contracts mature. The input is stated at base input costs (label above), with the Brent cost link applied on top of it by the engine, so the realised margin shown in the model is below the input by the un-passed-through share of any Brent move and the input is not double-counted. The long-run rate is the last actual, not a haircut below it; the mix effect is sourced from the half-year result.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Fuel and equipment rental sit inside operations of plant and equipment and rental of heavy equipment (US$194m and US$61m in FY2025 direct costs); we treat 5% of COGS as Brent-linked, a deliberately narrow share because most direct cost is subcontractors, labour and materials.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Half of the Brent-linked fuel/rental cost is assumed recovered through contract fuel-escalation clauses; mining-service contracts are quoted on indexed rates, but no disclosed clause quantifies the pass-through, so the pass-through is set at 0.50, the analyst's central case, and the remaining half of any Brent move is left to hit the margin line.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: SG&A plus final tax: FY2025 selling/admin was 5.05% of revenue and final tax 1.10%, but H1 2026 selling/admin ran at 3.7% of revenue as scale rose; 4.5% is the central full-year rate, not the FY2025 fixed-cost ratio.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated LK total D&A (depreciation 90.552 plus amortisation 14.605) was 11.86% of FY2025 revenue; H1 2026 D&A annualises at a similar rate as the enlarged fleet is depreciated. Held at 12.0% and eased to 11.0% as capex normalises.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was 49% of revenue in a fleet-expansion year; H1 2026 capex was US$47.1m (PP&E US$43.087m plus intangibles US$4.050m), 8.7% of H1 revenue, as the build completed and contracts mobilised. We hold the H1 run-rate at 8.7% for FY2026E (no sourced H2 step-up exists), then lift capex to 11% long run - in line with the 11% D&A ratio - so the enlarged fleet is maintained in real terms rather than run down. Sensitivity arithmetic — at FY2026E revenue, 1pp of capex/revenue is US$11.3m of annual FCF; across the ten explicit years its present value is about US$92.5m, roughly 31% of the US$296.2m DCF equity value, so the capex path is the largest single swing in the valuation. The engine's sensitivity grid has no capex axis, so this arithmetic is disclosed here and the report's DCF table lets the reader trace it.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was 12.6% of revenue; the H1 2026 ratio is distorted by the KMS related-party receivable, which converts to the SINI stake and cash in July 2026, so the normalised FY2025 ratio is held.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 income tax was 10.9% of PBT after the final tax already charged above EBIT; 12% keeps the LK's effective rate and allows for the non-deductible items shown in the tax note.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest expense of US$55.7m on average debt of US$623.6m is 8.9%; the disclosed IDR facilities price at IndONIA plus a margin and the bonds/sukuk carry fixed coupons (6.50%-9.50%), so 8.0% is the forward blended P&L cost. This is deliberately separate from the WACC debt leg, which the engine takes from the house macro deck as the USD risk-free rate plus the deck's 200bp corporate spread (6.93%, S12); the report discloses both rates and the WACC sensitivity table brackets the difference.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of US$2.7m on opening cash of US$114.9m is 2.35%; 2.0% allows for the restricted balances that earn less.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new net borrowing assumed: the KMS proceeds repay the Time Loan 2 and H1 2026 operating cash flow turns positive, so debt is held flat in the base case.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: No recurring other income assumed; FY2025's US$34.5m other gain is non-recurring (acquisition-related) and is not capitalised.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 minorities took 17.7% of net profit after the PTHDK/PTHDS acquisitions; H1 2026 minorities were negative during mobilisation. 10% is a smoothed central case between the FY2024 2.5% and FY2025 17.7%.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2024 and FY2025 dividends paid were 32% and 34% of parent net profit; the company has no fixed policy and the group has heavy capex and debt, so 35% is the central payout rather than the engine's 100% default.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No share change in the base case: the 170m-share rights issue is not final and still needs the 23 November 2026 EGM approval, so it is treated as a catalyst, not a base-case dilution.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.0% terminal growth for a USD-reporting contractor with life-of-mine contracts; below Indonesian nominal GDP and consistent with the house terminal-growth default, so no terminal value is created by an unsourced growth premium.

challenges.challenge: The thesis and sections 1 and 6 call the two 23 July 2026 Kapuas contracts (PBC US$431.2m, CBP US$89.6m) SINI-linked / SINI-affiliated entities and SINI a customer. S3 p.165 identifies PBC and CBP only as counterparties with no SINI link, the H1 related-party revenue note (F67) lists PBP/CUAN/ INPEX/TP and not PBC/CBP, and coverage/universe/konglo.yaml puts SINI in the Hapsoro group, not the Barito group. The affiliation is uncited and contradicted by the record.
challenges.answer: Deleted every SINI attribution. Section 1 and section 6 now describe the 23 July 2026 Kapuas contracts as third-party awards: the LK contract note names PBC and CBP only as counterparties with no affiliate, and the H1 2026 related-party revenue note lists other group counterparties and not them [S3]. The thesis no longer carries any affiliation [S3][S11].

challenges.challenge: Section 1 says the SINI transaction is an intra-group asset sale and cross-holding rather than an arms-length third-party deal. SINI is a Happy Hapsoro group company (fund record HAPSORO members include SINI), not a Prajogo/Barito affiliate; the KMS sale was a cross-group deal that created a 19.88% associate stake, and the related-party flag applies only to the post-deal relationship.
challenges.answer: Section 1 and section 6 now state the KMS sale is a cross-group deal, SINI being a Hapsoro-group company rather than a Barito affiliate, and confine the related-party flag to the post-deal associate stake and the KMS receivable [S11][S3].

challenges.challenge: Both cross-checks are applied to trailing FY2025A metrics that include the US$52.0m coal-sale revenue and its EBITDA from KMS, divested 30 June 2026 and absent from the forecast. The report notes the distortion but does not normalise it. With DCF Rp549, EV/EBITDA Rp1,537 and EV/Sales Rp1,133, the cross-checks supply 62.7% of the Rp883 blend; on the ex-KMS revenue base of US$834.4m the EV/Sales leg alone falls to about Rp993.
challenges.answer: The engine applies a peer multiple to the reported ltm metric, so the cross-checks cannot be re-run on an ex-KMS base without breaking the growth history; instead the EV/Sales weight is cut to 10 percent, the leg is labelled an upper bound, and the report now sets the KMS-inflated FY2025A base against the continuing base it overstates [S4][S0].

challenges.challenge: The DCF is discounted from the 30 June 2026 balance-sheet date (model market.bs_date 2026-06-30; FY2026E discount fraction 0.5038) while the price is 4 November 2026. The twelve-month value of Rp1,235 is therefore a June-2027 value compared with a November-2026 price (an eight-month horizon), and the 2.09x price/fundamental ratio mixes dates. Re-basing to the price date gives a target near Rp2,098 (TR about -6.8%), not Rp2,140.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now discloses the 30 June 2026 discount date against the 4 November 2026 price, states the eight-month horizon explicitly, and says rolling the value to the price date adds roughly four months of the cost of capital, which does not change the direction of the call; re-basing needs a full-year balance sheet not in the record [S3].

challenges.challenge: The 9.52x EV/EBITDA median is the midpoint of eight contributors with a 1.37x-48.09x spread (ATLA 26.9, DEWA 13.06, MYOH 1.37, PKPK 48.1, RUIS 6.27, SUNI 5.53, UNIQ 10.25, WINS 8.80). The report dismisses DEWA and PKPK as contracted utility or small-cap cash flows, but DEWA is Darma Henwa, a coal-mining contractor and a direct comparable. Excluding PKPK alone moves the median to 8.80x (leg about Rp1,325); excluding the two highest to 7.53x (about Rp955).
challenges.answer: ATLA and PKPK are excluded with a reason each (subsea inspection contractor; small cap on near-zero trailing EBITDA), DEWA and MYOH are retained as the direct coal-mining contractors, every contributor business is named in section 4, and the median is published on that cleaned contractor subset with the spread disclosed [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: The report says gross margin is 9.7% in FY2026E and recovers to the FY2025 actual 12.66% by 2030. The model gross-margin line is 8.96% in FY2026E, 10.28% in FY2027E and 12.44% in FY2030E, because the Brent cost link subtracts from the input. The driver the report describes is not the driver the model applies.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now separates the pre-link input from the realised line and gives the realised gross-margin path for FY2026E, FY2027E and FY2030E from the model, so the driver described is the one the engine applies [S4].

challenges.challenge: link1_pass is set to 0.600 but its own basis says Half of the Brent-linked fuel/rental cost is assumed recovered and 50% is the analyst central case. The value and the text disagree.
challenges.answer: link1_pass is set to 0.50, its basis text states a half pass-through as the central case, and section 3 calls it a half pass-through, so value, basis and prose agree [S4].

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA metric of US$162.9m is after final tax (US$9.7m reported inside operating costs; the report says so), while the peer multiples are standard pre-tax EBITDA; applying 9.52x to the after-tax figure understates the leg by about 6% (about Rp166/share; the leg is Rp1,703 on pre-tax EBITDA). On the other side, the same multiple is applied to a KMS-inflated trailing EBITDA and minorities are 10% against the FY2025 actual 17.7%.
challenges.answer: Section 3 and section 4 disclose that the trailing EBITDA metric is after the final tax reported inside operating costs, the EV/EBITDA weight falls to 25 percent and the leg is labelled a floor for that reason; the minority percentage is not a line that reaches value because the bridge deducts the 30 June 2026 balance-sheet minority [S4][S3].

challenges.challenge: The bear scenario adds a 5pp NWC drag but not a related-party receivable impairment: at 30 June 2026 related-party trade receivables were US$103.5m plus US$89.9m other current (F40/F42), 71% of parent equity of US$271.8m; a 25% impairment is about Rp87/share and a 50% one about Rp174. It also omits a covenant breach/acceleration (D/E 3.0x, EBITDA-to-debt-and-interest 115%, bonds 1.15x) and the ANZ HBS waiver precedent.
challenges.answer: The bear working-capital shock is now sized against the related-party book as worth more than a quarter impairment and as a permanent cash loss rather than a reversing write-off, and the covenant and acceleration case rides the cost-of-debt shock as a reset, a waiver fee and tighter amortisation [S3][S0].

challenges.challenge: All three konglo regimes keep a premium: bear Rp1,540 is 1.25x the Rp1,235 fundamental, base 1.67x, bull 2.33x. Even the bear never returns to fundamental value, so the full-closure downside (Rp1,235, -45% from Rp2,250) is absent from the scenarios, and the PTRO-specific case for the base 30% closure is a qualitative group-flow claim contradicted by a compliant 27.61% free float and unsupported by any traded-float or ADTV evidence.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now states the full-closure floor as the twelve-month fundamental value against the price, says the lens bear never reaches it, and explains that a full-closure row cannot be built because the compression schedule is a house-deck parameter; the group-flow case is stated with its evidence limit admitted [S10][S11].

challenges.challenge: The 19.88% SINI stake is carried at cost US$65.8m, 24% of parent equity, with no test against the SINI listed price or a draft fundamental and no bull case for a re-rating. The konglo card requires a sourced group-consistent mark for group holdings; cost is a placeholder, not a valuation.
challenges.answer: The bridge carries the 19.88 percent SINI stake at the November market quote, US$100.4m against US$65.8m cost, labelled provisional because SINI is not covered in house, and the post-balance-sheet review records the fallback to the subscription price if the mark fails [S0][S3].

challenges.challenge: The bull scenario adds only the mirrored +6pp revenue growth and +2.5pp margin. The HBS gold/copper contracts with Harmony, Newmont and St Barbara and the Petrindo captive pipeline (Tamtama, Global Bara Mandiri, MTU, Daya Bumindo) are called bull-case drivers in sections 1 and 5 but are not sized or included, and the disclosed PBC/CBP volumes (189m BCM/42Mt and 40m BCM/8Mt, S3 p.165) are not used to test the ramp.
challenges.answer: The bull now cites the disclosed PBC life-of-mine volumes against its contract value as the mechanism its mirrored growth shock proxies, and states plainly that HBS and the Petrindo pipeline stay out because neither carries a disclosed value [S3][S2].

challenges.challenge: The PTRO own five-year average of 22.5x is the model own-history mean with n=3 annual observations (model.own_history.ev_ebitda.n=3); the Newcastle 118.0 FY2027E vs 150.3 spot in section 2 has no S number and is not in the packet; the 1.00 unlevered beta is cited to S0 but is the industry-default config; and no pledged-share flag appears is a negative assurance the AR does not support.
challenges.answer: The own-history average is no longer the anchor, the Newcastle figures are removed and the deck link stated qualitatively with a citation, the beta is labelled the industry default rather than a company source, and the pledge assurance is replaced by an explicit statement that pledges were not verified [S12][S4].

challenges.challenge: The summary says the -4.9% expected return is including the modelled dividend stream, but dps12 is zero and FY2027E DPS is US$0.000113 (about Rp2), so the return is price-only; the 6,098-word update is 1.7x the 3,500-word ceiling for an update and buries a one-line data-artefact correction.
challenges.answer: The summary now gives the modelled dividend and says the return is price-only, and the report is cut from 6,098 to about 3,860 words; the residual above the guide is the konglo lens and the sourced evidence for these fourteen answers [S0].

challenges.challenge: §3 still says 'the link exposes 0.1 of COGS to Brent' via the raw {{in.link1_share}} token, but link1_share is 0.05 with 0.50 pass-through (fund record; packet basis). The prose therefore doubles the modelled cost exposure (QC Q1; judge NOTE, confidence 0.95).
challenges.answer: Section 3 now renders the input as 5.0% of COGS to Brent with a 50.0% pass-through via the pct filter, matching link1_share 0.05 and link1_pass 0.50 in assumptions and the engine [S4].

challenges.challenge: §2 states 'The house coal deck assumes a lower forward Newcastle path than today's spot' with no [S#], and fund record carries no coal-deck entry (S0-S12 only). The claim is substantively true (fund record newc FY2027E 118.0 vs spot 150.35) but it part-justifies the 8/7/5/4% growth moderation on an uncitable input, against the commodity card's requirement to state the through-cycle marker with a number and a source (QC Q2).
challenges.answer: Registered the house coal deck as S13 (fund record newc FY2027E 118.0 vs spot 150.35) and cited it in section 2 and in the revenue-growth basis; the post-2026 growth moderation now rests on cited RPO conversion plus the deck [S13].

challenges.challenge: §4 and fund record post_bs_review both say the current KMS receivable is excluded because 'the matching Time Loan is already in net debt'. S3 pp.104-105 shows Time Loan 2 was drawn only 13/17 July 2026 (US$84m) and repaid 24 July 2026, so it is not on the 30 June balance sheet and not in net debt. The bridge outcome is right but the stated reason is false, and the ~US$18.9m collection residual (about Rp34/share of DCF value) is left outside the bridge without a stated treatment (QC Q3).
challenges.answer: Section 4 and post_bs_review now give the actual sequence: the US$84.677m current receivable was collected 24 July 2026, the US$65.8m SINI subscription was paid 23 July, and the US$84m time loan drawn 13/17 July was repaid 24 July so it is not in 30 June net debt; the US$18.877m residual is in the bridge [S3].

challenges.challenge: §5 says the +7.5pp working-capital shock 'absorbs roughly all of a quarter' of the related-party book. 7.5% of FY2026E revenue US$1,134.7m = US$85.1m = 44% of the US$193.4m trade-plus-other-current related-party receivables (82% of the US$103.5m trade receivable alone), so the bear's severity is understated by nearly half (QC Q4).
challenges.answer: Section 5 now describes the +7.5pp working-capital shock as a little under half of the combined trade and other current related-party book, and most of the trade receivable alone, keeping the permanent-cash-loss framing [S3].

challenges.challenge: The §4 bridge and post_bs_review mark the 19.88% SINI stake (US$100.4m at the 6 Nov quote vs US$65.8m cost) at market inside fundamental value. SINI is an uncovered Hapsoro-group konglo name, and VAL_KONGLO_REGIME §4 says an uncovered konglo sibling 'must not be marked at market' because its regime premium then enters the parent's value; here it adds US$34.6m, about Rp60/share. It is not a cosmetic NOTE: carrying SINI at cost lowers the twelve-month fundamental value by about Rp60 and the lens target to roughly Rp1,950, an expected return near -13%, i.e. REDUCE under the -10% reduce_max_pct band, versus the published HOLD at -7.7%. No journal of the Director's sibling-coverage decision exists (QC Q5).
challenges.answer: Carried the SINI stake at cost (US$65.8m) with the 6 November quote disclosed as a sensitivity, per VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4. The engine re-derives the premium kept at 1.975 and gives target Rp2,065 and expected return -8.2%, inside the HOLD band, so no REDUCE is triggered; the Rp1,950 estimate held the premium multiple constant. The Director sibling-coverage decision is recorded in post_bs_review [S3][S11].

challenges.challenge: The FY2025A interest_expense line is 49.116 against the LK's US$55.699m (S4 p.14); the historical P&L does not foot by US$6.6m and the error is in the fact history the engine rebuilds from (QC Q7). The most-likely card requires wrong data to be restated, not modelled around.
challenges.answer: Added F87 (FY2025A interest and finance charges US$55.699m) and F88 (FY2024A US$25.897m) from S4 p.14; the two-year history now foots and the engine restates the line; section 3 notes the restatement [S4].

challenges.challenge: Residual evidence and process items left open: §1 and §7 call the FY2025 overburden and coal volumes 'both records' while S2 states no record high (Q6); the -2.1pp FY2026E EBITDA-margin calibration gap (FY2025A 18.37% vs model 16.27%) has no qc_justification (Q8); the report is 3,807 words against the 3,500 update ceiling (lint WARN).
challenges.answer: Dropped the unsourced both-records claim; added qc_justification calibration.ebitda_margin citing the H1 2026 8.65% gross margin and the Brent link [S3]; trimmed the report to 3,499 words, inside the 3,500 update ceiling [S2].

missing_bull_case.note: The bull is only the mirrored +6pp growth / +2.5pp margin shock: the HBS gold/copper contracts with Harmony, Newmont and St Barbara and the Petrindo captive pipeline are called bull-case drivers in section 1/5 but are never sized or put in the bull, and the 19.88% SINI stake sits at cost US$65.8m (24% of parent equity) with no mark-to-market or draft-fundamental test. C11, C12. Resolved: the bull carries the disclosed PBC volumes against the contract value as the ramp mechanism, and the report states that HBS and the Petrindo pipeline are excluded for want of disclosed contract values rather than included unsourced. C11 is met by marking the SINI stake at the November market quote.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear adds a working-capital drag but not a related-party receivable impairment (US$103.5m trade plus US$89.9m other current at 30 June 2026; a 25% hit is about Rp87/share) or a covenant breach/acceleration (D/E 3.0x, EBITDA cover 115%, bonds 1.15x), and even the lens bear leaves a 1.25x premium (Rp1,540), so the full-closure downside of Rp1,235 (-45%) is never stated. C9, C10. Resolved: the bear working-capital shock is sized as worth more than a quarter impairment of the related-party book and as a permanent cash loss, the covenant and acceleration case rides the cost-of-debt shock, and section 5 states the full-closure floor at the twelve-month fundamental value.

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers are broadly sourced (management company 2026 revenue, capex 8.7% H1 run-rate, margin recovery), but the stated gross margin is not the modelled one (input 9.7% vs model line 8.96% FY2026E and 12.44% FY2030E because of the Brent link), link1_pass is 0.600 while its basis says 50%, the 9.52x peer median is the midpoint of an eight-name 1.37x-48.09x spread, and minorities are 10% against the FY2025 actual 17.7%. C5, C6, C7, C8. Resolved: the pre-link input and the realised gross-margin path are now shown separately, link1_pass is 0.50 with matching prose, the peer median sits on a cleaned contractor subset with ATLA and PKPK excluded for stated reasons, and the minority is handled through the balance-sheet bridge.

evidence_and_citations.note: Load-bearing claims outrun their sources: the July 2026 PBC/CBP contracts are called SINI-linked and SINI-affiliated and SINI a customer, but S3 p.165 lists them as third-party counterparties and the related-party revenue note names PBP/CUAN/INPEX/TP, not PBC/CBP; the SINI sale is called intra-group though SINI is in the Hapsoro group; the five-year average of 22.5x is n=3; the Newcastle 118.0/150.3 figures carry no S number. C1, C2, C13. Resolved: the SINI attribution of PBC and CBP is deleted and they are described as third-party awards on the contract note, the KMS sale is stated as cross-group with the Hapsoro group cited, the own-history average is no longer the anchor and the uncited Newcastle figures are removed.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF-FCFF is the right primary for a contractor and the net-debt/minorities/associates bridge is correct, but both cross-checks use trailing FY2025A metrics that include the KMS coal-sales business the forecast excludes (and an EBITDA after final tax), they supply 62.7% of the Rp883 blend, the DCF is discounted from the 30 June 2026 balance-sheet date while the price is 4 November 2026, and the target is an eight-month value, not a twelve-month one. C3, C4, C8. Resolved: the EV/Sales weight is cut to 10 percent and the leg labelled an upper bound on the KMS-inflated base, EV/EBITDA is described as a floor after final tax, the discount-date mismatch is disclosed with its direction, and the hooks are named business by business.

bias_and_tone.note: The D&A restatement and the artefact diagnosis are fair, but the report says the -4.9% return is including the modelled dividend stream when dps12 is zero and FY2027E DPS is about Rp2; it calls the own-history multiple five-year and dismisses DEWA, a direct coal-mining contractor, as contracted utility to keep the median low; and the 6,098-word update is 1.7x the 3,500-word ceiling. C5, C13, C14. Resolved: the summary gives the modelled dividend and calls the return price-only, the own-history multiple is no longer described as five-year, DEWA is retained as a direct coal-mining contractor, and the report is cut from 6,098 to about 3,860 words.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The MINING_CONTRACTORS override is the right response to the provisional METALS_OTHER registry tag and the konglo overlay correctly applies no regime adjustment (free float 27.61%, no HSC, deletion or enforcement), but the only commodity driver is Brent (5% of COGS) while the revenue deceleration is justified by a Newcastle deck figure not in the packet or cited, and the fix lives in assumptions rather than the registry, so the next refresh can re-break it. C3, C13. Resolved: the Newcastle reference is removed and the coal-deck link is stated qualitatively with a citation, the MINING_CONTRACTORS override and the no-adjustment konglo overlay stand, and the reclassification is flagged to the Director as an assumptions-level fix.

conservatism_audit.note: Cautious: FY2025A EBITDA after final tax (US$9.7m) applied to pre-tax peer multiples (about Rp166/share low); DEWA 13.06x dropped from the median; the Time Loan netting leaves about US$18.9m out of the bridge. Optimistic: the same multiple on KMS-inflated trailing EBITDA; minorities at 10% vs 17.7% actual; the prose 9.7% to 12.66% margin path vs the modelled 8.96% to 12.44%. Shocks are mirrored (+/-6pp growth, 2.5pp margin, 150bp debt, 5pp NWC) and base probability is 50%. C5, C6, C8. Resolved: the after-final-tax EBITDA is disclosed and its leg labelled a floor, DEWA is back in the median, the KMS-inflated base is disclosed as the reason EV/Sales is weighted at 10 percent, and the gross-margin prose now matches the modelled path.

calibration.note: FY2026E EBITDA margin is 16.46% against the FY2025A actual 18.37% (-1.91pp) and no qc_justification answers the calibration gap; the H1 2026 print (gross margin 8.65%, EBIT US$21.6m after a US$15.0m other gain) supports part of the step, but the report gross-margin path is the pre-Brent-link input, so the driver it describes is not the one modelled. C6. Resolved: the report no longer presents the pre-link input as the modelled gross margin, the realised path is shown for FY2026E through FY2030E, and the H1 2026 print is cited as partial support for the FY2026E step.

signoff.notes: Round 2 sign-off. Every round-1 L1-L7 and QC item is answered on substance and cured in the pack: SINI carried at cost per VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4 with the market quote demoted to a sensitivity (L5); FY2025A and FY2024A interest restated to 55.699 and 25.897 as F87/F88 so the history foots (L6); the Time Loan 2 reason corrected to the 13 and 17 July draw and the 24 July repayment (L3); the link renders as 5.0% of COGS with 50.0% pass-through (L1); the NWC shock is stated as a little under half the combined related-party book (L4); the house coal deck is registered and cited as S13 (L2); the report is 3,498 words and the -2.1pp calibration gap is justified on the H1 2026 8.65% gross margin (L7). The second QC audit PASSED with bias neutral and the judge PASSed at 0.94; no FATAL or MATERIAL item is open, and this is a single name so no shared-input tilt test applies. The remaining QC items are documentation-level and valuation-neutral (QC itself records valuation unaffected either way), so they do not block; the analyst must clear them at the next scheduled update: (1) register a market-data source for the 6 November 2026 SINI quote in the bridge label and post_bs_review, or delete the Rp7,600 / US$100.4m label and the US$34.6m / Rp60 sensitivity; (2) restate qc_justifications.konglo.overlay to 2.47x / Rp912.1 / Rp1,967 / Rp2,065 / Rp1,046; (3) in section 6 attach 6.8% to the trade receivable alone or state the combined US$193.4m book at about 12.7% of assets and 60% of total equity; (4) restate the capex-sensitivity basis against the engine DCF equity value of about US$311m; (5) drop the phrase a record order book from the summary and say low-to-mid single-digit ROE except 11% in FY2025. The HOLD at Rp2,065 and E(R) of -8.2% is the most likely call, not a cautious one: fundamental value today is Rp687, the probability-weighted twelve-month business value is Rp1,046, and the house konglo lens keeps 1.975x of the log premium for twelve months because the premium shows no compression trigger (free float 27.6% and compliant, no HSC listing, no index deletion, no enforcement on record); -8.2% sits inside the HOLD band and the full-closure downside is disclosed in section 5, so neither REDUCE nor BUY is better supported by the record.

bias.note: Base anchored on the management 2026 revenue expectation (US$1,135m, S4 p.118) and on H1 2026 actuals: gross-margin input 9.7% against H1 8.65% (S3 p.12), capex 8.7% of revenue vs H1 8.7%, opex 4.5% vs H1 4.68% (US$20.1m SG&A plus US$5.4m final tax on US$544.0m revenue). The only unsupported drifts are mildly optimistic and immaterial: opex about 0.2pp low and cost of debt 8.0% vs FY2025 8.9% (bonds 6.5-9.5%, S4), together under US$5m of EBIT. No default haircut: volumes held, capex not lifted above the H1 run-rate, no terminal-value growth premium. Scenarios mirrored on the same four drivers (growth +-6pp, margin +-2.5pp, debt cost -+1.5pp, NWC +-7.5pp) at 50/25/25. The 2.47x price-to-value gap is the house lens, not a biased fundamental.

findings.finding: The SINI sensitivity number is unsourced. The bridge item cites S3 for the US$65.8m cost fact (F28), but the Rp7,600 / US$100.4m quote dated 6 Nov 2026 in the bridge label, the post_bs_review note and section 4 has no market-price source: S3 is the 30 June 2026 LK with no market price, S11 is the konglo registry with no price, and no fact records the quote. The Rp60/share sensitivity is therefore unverifiable.

fund record qc_justifications.konglo.overlay quotes pre-fix lens figures: price 2.40x a probability-weighted fundamental today of Rp935.7 (log 0.88), base regime Rp1,983, target Rp2,076 and twelve-month fundamental Rp1,073. After SINI is carried at cost the engine gives 2.47x, Rp912.1 (log 0.90), base regime Rp1,967, target Rp2,065 and twelve-month fundamental Rp1,046, and sections 4-5 match the engine. A justification answering a house-law gate must state what the gate now produces.

Section 6 reads that related-party trade receivables were US$103.5m plus US$89.9m of other current, 6.8% of consolidated assets. The 6.77% in F65/S3 is the US$103.5m trade receivable alone as a share of consolidated assets; the combined US$193.4m book is about 12.7% of assets, 60% of total equity and 71% of parent equity. The sentence attaches the trade-only ratio to the combined book.

The assumptions capex basis quotes a DCF equity value of US$296.2m, but the engine DCF leg is Rp559 per share on 10,086.05m shares, about US$311m (EV 987.1 less net debt 740.1, minorities 49.5, plus associates 16.9 and bridge 97.0). The US$92.5m present-value arithmetic is sound; only its denominator is stale.
